title: AI Mock — Paper 1 (Sections 1–4)
instructions: AI-generated progress test in the style of a 9618 Paper 1. Answer all questions. Calculators are not permitted.

questions.text: Which binary prefix represents **2⁴⁰** bytes?
questions.explanation: Ki = 2¹⁰, Mi = 2²⁰, Gi = 2³⁰, Ti = 2⁴⁰. Decimal prefixes (kilo, mega, giga, tera) use powers of 10.

questions.text: Convert **-45** to 8-bit two's complement binary. Show your working.
Why is **BCD** used in some systems, such as a digital clock display?

options.text: Each denary digit is stored separately, making display of denary digits simple
It stores more values per byte than binary
It is the same as hexadecimal

questions.explanation: In BCD each 4 bits holds one denary digit 0–9, so displaying denary digits needs no conversion — useful for clocks, meters and calculators. It is less efficient for arithmetic.

questions.text: Sound is sampled at 44.1 kHz with a resolution of 16 bits, for 10 seconds. How many **bits** of data are produced? Give the value in **kilobits (kb, 1 kb = 1000 bits)**, to 1 decimal place.
Which pair consists of **only** lossless compression formats?
questions.explanation: PNG (image) and FLAC (audio) are lossless. JPEG and MP3 are lossy.

questions.text: An image 800 × 600 pixels has a colour depth of 24 bits. Calculate the uncompressed file size in **MiB**, to 2 decimal places.
Which protocol is used to **securely** transfer web pages?
questions.explanation: HTTPS = HTTP over TLS/SSL, so the data is encrypted in transit.

questions.text: Explain the difference between **bit streaming** (real-time) and **downloading** a video file, and give one advantage of bit streaming.

answer.text: Downloading: the whole file is copied to local storage before it can be used.
Bit streaming: data is sent as a continuous stream and played as it arrives, using a buffer.
Real-time streaming sends at the rate needed for playback / with no local file kept; on-demand streaming can be paused and seeked.
Advantage: no need to wait for the full download, no large local storage needed, content can be protected from copying.

questions.explanation: Mentioning the buffer (to absorb variation in network speed) usually earns a mark.

questions.text: What is the main function of a **NIC (network interface card)**?

options.text: To connect a device to a network and convert data into signals for the transmission medium
To resolve domain names into IP addresses

questions.explanation: The NIC provides the physical connection and has a unique MAC address.

questions.text: Explain what a **thin client** is and state **two** benefits of thin clients for a business.

answer.text: A thin client is a low-specification terminal that relies on a powerful server for processing and storage.
Cheaper hardware, less maintenance/upgrading needed on each client.
Improved security — data is kept on the server, not on the device; easier central backup/management.

questions.explanation: Disadvantages: total dependence on the server/network; heavy server load. Do not confuse with a thick(client) PC.

questions.text: Which of these is an **output** device only?
questions.explanation: A plotter draws large technical drawings/graphs — output only.

questions.text: A **NOR** gate has inputs A = 0 and B = 0. State the output and explain how it is derived.

answer.text: A OR B = 0, and NOR inverts it, so output = 1.

questions.explanation: NOR gives 1 only when ALL inputs are 0.

questions.text: Complete the truth table for **X = NOT (A AND B) OR C**.
questions.explanation: X is 0 only for the single row A=1, B=1, C=0.

questions.text: Describe how a **touch screen** detects input, distinguishing between **capacitive** and **resistive** technology.

answer.text: Resistive: two layers separated by a small gap; pressing makes them touch and changes the resistance, giving the x/y position. It needs pressure.
Capacitive: a grid/film holds an electrical charge; the finger (a conductor) changes the capacitance at that point, which is detected.
Capacitive is multi-touch and often more responsive; resistive works with a stylus or gloved hand and is cheaper.

questions.explanation: The exam often also expects: the processor converts the coordinates to a screen position and the application responds.

questions.text: In the FDE cycle, which register holds the address of the next instruction to be fetched?
questions.explanation: PC → MAR → memory. The MDR holds the data/instruction fetched; CIR holds the instruction being decoded.

questions.text: In the 9618 instruction set, which mnemonic loads the **contents of a memory address** into the accumulator?
questions.explanation: LDD = load immediate data; LDM = load from a direct memory address; LDI = indirect; LDX = indexed.

questions.text:
A byte contains **1011 0110**. Perform the following bit manipulations and give each result as an 8-bit binary number.

**(a)** AND with 0000 1111 (mask)
**(b)** OR with 0000 1111
**(c)** XOR with 1111 1111
**(d)** shift left by 2
questions.explanation: (d) shifting left by 2 discards the two most significant bits (10) and fills with 0s: 1101 1000.

questions.text: Which statement best describes an **interrupt**?

options.text: A signal that causes the processor to temporarily stop the current program and run an interrupt service routine
A permanent error that stops the computer

questions.explanation: Interrupts allow the CPU to respond to events (e.g. key press, I/O complete) without polling.

questions.text: Write assembly language to compute **Z = X − Y** where X is at address 400 and Y is at address 401, storing the result at address 402.

answer.text: LDM 400
SUB 401 (subtracts the contents of address 401)
STO 402

questions.explanation:
LDM 400
SUB 401
STO 402

Note that if address 401 is not a valid operand for SUB in your table, use LDM 401 into another register and subtract registers.

questions.text: Explain **two** advantages of **parallel processing** compared with serial processing.

answer.text: Multiple tasks (or parts of a task) are executed at the same time, reducing total processing time.
Better throughput / a large task can be split into independent sub-tasks; or greater resilience (if one processor fails, work can be redistributed).

questions.explanation: Include 'simultaneously / at the same time' for the first mark. Disadvantages: cost, coordination overhead, not all tasks can be parallelised.
